questions.stem: Per this page, which situation justifies a Strategy pattern, an interface with a separate class for each variant?

options.text: One processor is in use today, and two more may be added someday
options.says: The page says complexity justified by "what if" or "someday we might" is almost always premature; with one processor the pattern is not justified.

options.text: Three processors are in use today, and each one already takes payments
options.says: The page says a strategy pattern is justified when you have three different payment processors today.

options.text: One validation rule is in use today, and more callers may reuse it
options.says: The page names the Strategy pattern for a single validation rule as a KISS violation.

questions.stem: `isValidUsername` and `isValidProductCode` apply the same length rule today. What does this page advise?

options.text: Merge them into one generic method, since their rule is identical today
options.says: The page says over-applied DRY would merge them, and that KISS keeps them separate.

options.text: Replace both with a rule framework, since its rules could be reused later
options.says: The page names rule frameworks for simple checks as over-engineering.

options.text: Keep them as two methods, since their domains may diverge over time
options.says: The page says they serve different domains and may diverge, so keeping them separate is simpler.
